thread:
Noah: Idea: build a lightweight 'Fallback Jury' that treats the fallback decision like a voting quorum across cheap probes (latency delta, error-rate spike, backend timeouts, recent rollback counts, and a tiny quality probe). It returns a single jury_score 0..1. Reduce flapping by requiring weighted quorum + time decay.
Priya: interesting metaphor. how is this different from a single composite score (e.g., weighted sum)?
Noah: two differences: (1) we keep probe autonomy
nd let each probe cast a vote (+/- with confidence) instead of forcing raw normalization into one noisy number, (2) quorum rules let us require orthogonal probe agreement for fast action (avoid acting on just error-rate blips).
Sam: runtime placement? proxy sidecar, central service, or both?
Noah: hybrid. local jury in proxy for sub-second decisions (5-30s windows) and a central jury aggregator for cohort-wide adjudication. Local jury votes fast; central jury used for cross-region rollbacks.
jenkins-bot: ci/checks: created job fallback-jury/proto-smoke.
sre-bot: ticket SRE-5007 created: fallback-jury runbook + alert mapping.
Priya: what are input probes? keep it cheap.
Noah: p95 latency delta, error-rate delta, quick synthetic quality probe (if available), queue depth delta, and recent fallback events. Each probe returns {state:ok/warn/bad, confidence:0..1}. Jury applies a simple rule: if weighted_bad_votes >= quorum_threshold -> jury_score drops below action threshold.
Sam: contract with fallback controller?
Noah: simple HTTP contract: POST /v1/jury/evaluate {cohort, raw_signals} -> {jury_score, window_ms, top_votes}. Decision controller uses jury_score and a TTL. If jury_score < rollback_threshold persistently for decay_window -> trigger rollback.
Priya: explainability is key. UI must show top_votes that drove decision.
Noah: yes: jury returns top_votes as small list e.g. ["p95:+42% (0.9)","errors:+1.2% (0.7)"] so Console shows human-readable drivers.
Sam: failure modes? if jury service is down we should fail-open.
Noah: agree. fallback-controller falls back to legacy heuristics and emits incident. Local jury in proxy is optional feature-flag; if it crashes we pass-through and mark `jury_pass_through=true` in telemetry.
Priya: performance hit?
Noah: local jury is intended to be stateless streaming aggregates (rolling counters) with O(1) cost per request. median latency impact <1ms. Central aggregator consumes periodic summaries every 10s. No per-request RPC to central in the fast path.
Sam: signal cardinality concerns? cohorts x models can be many.
Noah: store fixed-size windows keyed by (cohort, model_class). Use streaming sketches for quantiles where needed. Expose aggregate metrics: jury.input_votes, jury.bad_votes, jury.score.p50/p95, jury.top_drivers.
jenkins-bot: note: added integration test that simulates a 30s microburst and verifies no immediate rollback if only one probe is noisy.
sre-bot: runbook note: emergency kill-switch env var FALLBACK_JURY=off and feature flag fallback_jury.global.disable. Also add escalation path if central aggregator lags >30s.
Priya: rollout plan: opt-in per-route -> sidecar local jury at 1% cohorts for 3 days -> 5% for 2 weeks -> central aggregator enabled for those cohorts. Monitor false-negative and false-positive rates.
Noah: tradeoffs: + avoids rollback churn, + explainable drivers, + orthogonal-signal safety; - adds policy surface, - needs ops on metrics and dashboarding.
Sam: thumbs up. can you mock the minimal POST payload for the RFC?
Noah: sure: `POST /v1/jury/evaluate` body: `cohort:pilot-42, window_ms:30000, probes:[{"name":"p95_latency","delta":42.1,"conf":0.9},{"name":"err_rate","delta":1.2,"conf":0.7}]` response: `jury_score:0.28, top_votes:["p95_latency:+42%(0.9)","err_rate:+1.2%(0.7)"]`. I'll draft the RFC with sequence diagrams, config knobs (quorum_threshold, vote_weights, decay_ms), and Console wireframes. pinging @eng-sre @eng-platform for review. :mag:
